name: Virginia Foxx

items.text: In April 2009, during House debate on the Matthew Shepard hate crimes bill, Foxx said Shepard was killed in a robbery, not because he was gay. She called the bill's use of his case a "hoax." She later said "hoax" was a poor choice of words and his death was a tragedy. She said she relied on two news reports.
items.why: This was a floor remark on a bill that she partly walked back, with no finding of wrongdoing and no clear bearing on any criterion.

items.text: After the Jan. 6 Capitol attack, a Capitol Police report said Foxx set off a House chamber metal detector, threw her bag under a table and went in to vote despite two officers trying to stop her. She was fined $5,000. She wrote that she disputed the facts. The House Ethics Committee dropped the fine.
items.why: The fine was dropped on appeal, so no official finding of an ethics violation stands, and the screening rule is a minor security matter under the abuse-of-position criterion.
Shouting "shut up" and "go away" at a reporter at a press conference is a petty moment of temper, not conduct bearing on any criterion.

for_review: Item 3: the Washington Times and The Hill pages would not open, so I judged it from search-result excerpts only (Washington Times, The Hill, Fox59, Guardian, Fox News). Those excerpts agree she said 'shut up' and 'go away'. Item 2: the Forbes page returned only navigation, and I did not read the House Ethics Committee notice or the Capitol Police report directly. I also did not confirm the exact dates of the fine and the dismissal; The Hill page gives no year. The Hill and other coverage say the Ethics Committee dropped the fine because she disputed the facts. Item 1: the 2009 remark is her own words and was widely criticized, and she retracted only the word 'hoax'. She did not retract the claim that the killing was a robbery. I rated it context because it has no clear bearing on any criterion. A reviewer could treat it as leave_off instead. The owner-site search (alexjoneslive.com, stewpeters.com, ryandawson.org, infowars.com) returned nothing about Foxx. No other items were found that meet the against or open bar. I did not search for AIPAC or foreign-travel records, since a separate step covers them. Attendance was not weighed.
